scope: Proposition 4.2 (Odd coefficients under a genus-index bound) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume that a constant C∗ satisfies j(PD) ≥ w(D) + 1 2s(h) − C∗ (4.6) for every h in the filter with a simple zero. There are arbitrarily large precisions M, good odd primes ℓ outside the fixed support, and holomorphic weight-3/2 forms gM = P aM (n)qn, of level supported on S ∪ {ℓ}, with the following properties. (i) The additional filter at ℓ is (h∗/ℓ) = −σ, (h/ℓ) = σ, ρT (Frℓ) ≡ C (mod 2M ), (4.7) where C is the action of a complex conjugation. In particular ℓ ≡ −1 (mod 2M ). (ii) After a fixed harmless decrease in the working precision, the forms satisfy Equa- tion (4.1) modulo that precision, with characters ηM , ψM of 2-power order and quadratic ratio. Their squarefree coefficients have the form of a 2-power phase times an integer modulo 2M . (iii) If a coefficient is visible, meaning v(aM (D)) < M, then E(h) has a simple zero and j(PD) ≤ v(aM (D)) + C1. (4.8) For every admissible D the coefficient lower bound is v(aM (D)) ≥ min{M, w(D) + 1 2s(h) − C2} (4.9) when the product derivative is nonzero; if it is zero, the coefficient is zero modulo 2M . Here C1, C2 are independent of ℓ, M, D. (iv) A fixed squarefree witness Dw in the original filter is admissible at every chosen ℓ and has v(aM (Dw)) bounded as M → ∞. For irreducible E[2], the hypothesis is Theorem 3.6. For rational two-torsion, the positive filters used in the pointwise argument have this bound by Proposition 7.7, using only the even source. An arbitrary twist is first absorbed into the fixed curve, so only these positive filters are needed there.
